name: Question 2
problem: Find the orthogonal projection matrix that maps $x\in {R}^{2}$ onto the subspace spanned by an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-1$ of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

Moreover, ${u}_{i}\cdot {u}_{i}^{T}$ is the projection matrix corresponding to ${u}_{i}.$

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda =-1.$ Computing $A-(-1)I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A+1I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]+1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations which is already in row echelon form and has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=0.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],
$$

where $‖v‖=1.$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: 

$$
u=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {u}^{T} & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

Moreover, ui⋅uiT is the projection matrix corresponding to ui.

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to λ=−1. Computing A−(−1)I, we get

A+1I=[200−1]+1[1001]=[3000].

So, we have a system of linear equations which is already in row echelon form and has one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=0. Hence, the general solution is

[0x2],x2∈R.

Therefore, setting x2=1, we get the eigenvector

v=[01],

where ‖v‖=1. Dividing v by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: u=v‖v‖=[01]

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

u⋅uT=[01]⋅[01]=[01]⋅[01]=[0001].
